title: Decision curve analysis: net benefit of a prediction model
summary: Net benefit of treating by a model's predicted risk at prespecified thresholds, against treating everyone and treating no one.

sizing._why: Decision curves are not sized on their own; the model's validation sample size governs.

pinned_defaults: Net benefit = TP/n - FP/n x t / (1 - t), treating when predicted risk exceeds t; treat-all = prevalence - (1 - prevalence) t / (1 - t); treat-none = 0.
Thresholds prespecified from the clinical decision (0.1, 0.2, 0.3); the whole curve over that range should be plotted. Written out in both languages; R's dcurves draws the same quantity.
_reading: A model is useful at a threshold only if it beats both default strategies. Here it beats treat-all clearly at 0.2 and 0.3 and only slightly at 0.1.
